_about: Generated by tools/update-catalogue.js from docs/reference/validation-catalogue.md, the Markdown export of the catalogue document. Do not edit: change the document, export it again and run the script.
title: Payments Validator – pain.001 Validation Catalogue (Phase 1)
lead: Updated on 28 Nov 2026 to match the Testing Portal 0.4.0-m3, whose rules follow this catalogue as confirmed on 18 Nov 2026. Of the 145 checks, the app builds 134, and 15 of those find nothing until a setting changes. Four are covered by other checks, 7 are not built, and the app adds 2.x and X.1.

blocks.p: The validator runs 11 stages in a fixed order, and only Stages 0 and 1 stop the run. Without well-formed XML and a known pain.001 version nothing else can be evaluated. From Stage 2 onwards every check runs on the parsed file and all findings are returned in one report.

head: Stage
What it checks
On failure
rows: Size, encoding, well-formed XML, XML security
Namespace, version, message type, version allowed for the selected country
Structure, order, cardinality, data types, code enumerations
Selected country vs file content, payment type of each transaction
Totals, dates, amounts, cross-field rules, external code lists
Allowed characters, identifiers, IBAN, BIC, reference formats
Bank rules stricter than XSD: mandatory, forbidden, lengths, limits
Rules of the country the customer selected
Truncation, ignored fields, non-business days, recommendations

blocks.p: How the report shows all findings at once:

ul: XSD errors do not stop the run. The business rules run on the same parsed document; a rule whose element is missing simply does not fire, which avoids most cascades.
Consequential findings are suppressed and linked to their root. Example: an IBAN that already failed the XSD pattern is not checked again for checksum or country.
Repeated findings are grouped: one rule failing on 4,000 transactions is one finding with a count and the list of locations.
Every finding carries rule ID, severity, ISO status reason code, level (file, payment block, transaction), XPath plus line and column, actual value, expected value and a fix hint.
Severity: Error means CMIplus would reject; Warning means it would be processed but changed, truncated, ignored or is risky; Info is advice.

Known limit: after a structural XSD error the parser may skip the rest of that parent element, so findings inside a badly broken block can be incomplete. The report says so for that block. In the app the XSD check repairs the parsed file and checks it again, up to 8 times, so later errors are still found; it stops after 5,000 XSD errors.

blocks.p: In the tables below, Severity is the proposed default (E = Error, W = Warning, I = Info) and the code is the ISO 20022 status reason code proposed for the pain.002-like result. Both are to be confirmed against actual CMIplus behaviour.

The In the app column says what the Testing Portal does with each check. Yes: it runs, with the values it uses. Off: it is built, but finds nothing with the current settings. Covered by: another check reports the same problem. Not built: with the reason. Decisions made since 18 Nov are listed under Decisions after confirmation.

The Built in column says where the check is implemented in the app. JavaScript: in the app's own code. XML parser and XSD: by the libxml2 parser with the pain.001 XSD schema. Schematron: in the Schematron rule files; JavaScript only reads settings, code lists or the date. Schematron + JS: a Schematron rule that calls a JavaScript function for part of the check, named after the colon. The Schematron rules run in the browser with SaxonJS.
Stage 0 decides whether the upload can be parsed at all; any failure ends the run with one fatal finding that names the line and column.

rows.check: File uploaded and not empty
File size within the configured limit
rows.app: Yes, 20 MB (browser limit; the CMIplus limit is not known)

rows.check: Single XML file, not an archive or other file type
rows.app: Yes, also detects ZIP, PDF, Office and HTML files

rows.check: Malware scan passed
rows.app: Not built: not possible in the browser

rows.check: Encoding is UTF-8, the declared encoding matches the bytes, no invalid byte sequences

rows.app: Not built: needs what CMIplus expects

rows.check: Well-formed XML: one root, matching tags, escaped &, < and quotes
No DOCTYPE, no external entities, entity expansion within limits (XXE protection)
No content after the root element, such as two messages concatenated

blocks.p: The parser message is translated into a fix hint, for example "Unescaped & on line 245, column 31: replace with &".
Stage 1 detects the message and version, which selects the XSD for Stage 2 and the rule-set variant for Stages 4–8.

rows.check: Root element is Document
Namespace is pain.001.001.03 (ISO 2009) or pain.001.001.09 (ISO 2019)
Message element is CstmrCdtTrfInitn
Detected version is accepted by CMIplus for the selected country
rows.app: Yes; .03 and .09 accepted for all 11 countries until confirmed

rows.check: Namespace prefixes and xsi:schemaLocation used as CMIplus accepts
rows.app: Not built: needs what CMIplus accepts

rows.check: Version still supported but scheduled for retirement (if CMIplus announces one)
rows.app: Not built: needs a CMIplus announcement

blocks.p: Other recognised messages get a specific hint instead of a generic error, for example "This is a pain.008 direct debit file" or "This is pain.001.001.05, which is not supported".
Stage 2 validates against the official ISO schema of the detected version and keeps going after each error, so all structural findings are listed together.

rows.check: Elements appear in the order the schema defines
Mandatory elements present (schema minimum occurrence)
Maximum occurrences not exceeded
No unknown, misspelled or wrong-namespace elements or attributes
Exactly one option of each choice, e.g. IBAN or Othr, InstdAmt or EqvtAmt
Text within the schema length (Max35Text, Max70Text, Max140Text) and not empty
Pattern types valid: BIC, IBAN, country code, currency code; in .09 also UETR and LEI
Schema enumerations valid: payment method, charge bearer, priority
Amounts: max 18 digits and 5 decimals, not negative, currency attribute present
Dates and date-times in ISO format
Boolean values valid (e.g. BtchBookg)
Any other schema error that 2.1–2.11 do not name

blocks.p: Version differences handled by the two schemas: .09 renames BIC to BICFI, makes the execution date a choice of Dt or DtTm, and adds structured address elements. External code lists (purpose, category purpose, service level, local instrument) are free text in the schema and are checked in Stage 4.
Stage 3 checks that the file fits the country the customer selected and assigns a payment type to every transaction; that type decides which Stage 7 and Stage 8 rules run.

rows.check: Selected country has a configured rule pack
rows.app: Yes; always passes for the 11 countries

rows.check: Debtor account IBAN country matches the selected country
Debtor agent BIC country (characters 5–6) matches the selected country
All payment blocks belong to the selected country, if CMIplus requires one country per file
rows.app: Yes, one country per file; reported only when 3.2 and 3.3 are switched off

rows.check: Payment type can be determined for each transaction
Payment type is supported in the selected country
rows.app: Yes; every type is offered, SEPA types only in SEPA countries

rows.check: One payment type per payment block, if CMIplus requires it
rows.app: Yes, one type per block; intra-bank and budget payments do not make a block mixed

blocks.p: Payment types: SEPA credit transfer, SEPA Instant, domestic standard, domestic urgent, cross-border (SWIFT), intra-bank transfer, budget or tax payment. They are derived from service level, local instrument, category purpose, currency, and the creditor account and agent country. The derived type is shown per transaction in the report, so a customer sees why a rule applied.
In the app a transaction gets the first type that applies, in this order:

ol: SEPA credit transfer: service level SEPA.
Budget or tax payment: category purpose TAXS, GOVT, VATX, WHLD or SSBE, or a treasury account (RO: TREZ in the IBAN), with the creditor in the selected country or unknown.
Intra-bank transfer: creditor in the selected country and creditor agent BIC (first 8 characters) the same as the debtor agent's.
SEPA credit transfer: EUR between SEPA countries, without any service level and not urgent.
Domestic urgent: creditor in the selected country, with service level URGP or SDVA or priority HIGH.
Domestic standard: creditor in the selected country.
Cross-border (SWIFT): creditor country known and not the selected country.

blocks.p: A transaction that fits none of them gets finding 3.5. The creditor country comes from the creditor IBAN, else the creditor agent BIC, else the creditor address.
Stage 4 holds the cross-field rules that apply to every pain.001 regardless of country, ordered by message level.

sections.title: Character set, identifiers and field formats

blocks.p: Stage 5 checks every text and identifier value against the character set of its payment type and the algorithmic formats (check digits, registries) that the XSD pattern cannot verify.

rows.check: Text uses the allowed character set: SEPA Latin set (a–z A–Z 0–9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' + space), SWIFT X set for cross-border, local letters only where CMIplus allows
rows.app: Yes: SEPA Latin for SEPA, SWIFT X for cross-border, basic Latin for the other payments in all 11 countries; dates, amounts, IBANs, BICs and codes are left to the XSD

rows.check: Characters CMIplus would transliterate (e.g. ä to a)
No control characters, tabs or line breaks inside values
No leading or trailing spaces, no whitespace-only values
rows.app: Yes; blank ids and creditor names are reported by 4.1, 4.6, 4.20 and 4.28

rows.check: Reference IDs (MsgId, PmtInfId, InstrId, EndToEndId) do not start or end with "/" and contain no "//"
IBAN country known, length per IBAN registry, mod-97 check digits, national BBAN structure
rows.app: Yes: AC02 for the debtor, AC03 for the creditor; the charges account IBAN is reported by 4.18

rows.check: BIC is 8 or 11 characters with a valid country code
Test BIC ("0" as second location character) used in a production file
BIC found in the BIC directory (static reference file)
rows.app: Not built: needs the licensed BIC directory

rows.check: Country codes valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, plus XK where used for Kosovo
rows.app: Yes; the creditor country is reported by 4.29, the regulatory reporting country by 4.40

rows.check: LEI (in .09) has 20 characters and valid ISO 17442 check digits
Organisation and private ID scheme codes in the ISO external lists

blocks.p: The IBAN, BIC and country checks run on every party and agent: debtor, creditor, ultimate parties, charges account and intermediary agents. The reason code follows the party, e.g. AC02 for the debtor account and AC03 for the creditor account.
Stage 6 applies RBI's own pain.001 guideline for CMIplus, which tightens the ISO schema; these rules come from the CMIplus usage guideline, not from ISO.

rows.check: Elements mandatory in the CMIplus guideline but optional in the XSD
rows.app: Off: no mandatory elements set yet

rows.check: Elements not supported by CMIplus: forbidden (error) or ignored (warning)
rows.app: Off: no forbidden or ignored elements set yet

rows.check: Occurrence limits stricter than the XSD (e.g. 1 Ustrd, 2 AdrLine)
rows.app: Yes: max 2 AdrLine in every address; the number of Ustrd is checked by 4.38

rows.check: Length limits stricter than the XSD (e.g. names 70, remittance 140)
rows.app: Yes: names max 70; 140 for remittance is the XSD limit

rows.check: Maximum payment blocks per file and transactions per file and per block
Currency supported for the selected country and payment type
rows.app: Off: no currency lists in the country files; 7.1, 7.10 and 7.13 check the currency

rows.check: Execution date horizon and past-date handling as configured in CMIplus
Batch booking value allowed and its conditions met (e.g. one currency per block)
rows.app: Yes: batch booking allowed, one currency per block

rows.check: Code values within the subset CMIplus supports (purpose, category purpose, service level, local instrument)
rows.app: Off: every ISO code is allowed until the CMIplus subset is set

rows.check: Initiating party identification in the format CMIplus expects
Multiple debtor accounts or debtor agents in one file only if allowed
rows.app: Off: both allowed for now; agents are compared by the first 8 characters of the BIC

rows.check: Ultimate debtor and ultimate creditor only where supported

blocks.p: Keep these rules in a separate module from the ISO rules so a guideline change never touches the ISO layer.

Stage 7 runs the scheme rules for the payment type assigned in Stage 3. Unstructured postal addresses stay accepted for now. The EPC postponed the SEPA end date of 15 November 2026 ([EPC](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/node/28486)) and will set a new one by February 2027 ([Banking 4.0](https://banking40.ro/european-payments-council-defers-setting-new-end-date-for-unstructured-address-format-until-february-2027/)). Swift deferred the CBPR+ removal planned for 14 November 2026 and has not set a new date ([Swift](https://www.swift.com/insights/news/swift-accepts-community-request-extend-structured-address-migration-iso-20022-payment-messages)). Checks 7.8 and 7.18 are warnings until new end dates are set.

Budget, tax and customs payments: detected by creditor account or category purpose, checked in Stage 8

blocks.p: The pack of the selected country runs on top of all generic rules and may only tighten them, never relax them. Its content comes from each network bank's local CMIplus guideline; every pack covers the same ten categories.

head: Category
Typical checks
rows: Non-IBAN domestic account format and check digits; local IBAN length and BBAN structure
Bank or sort code exists in the static local bank directory and matches the IBAN bank code and BIC
Local currency, decimals, maximum amounts, high-value thresholds
Allowed combinations of service level, local instrument and category purpose for standard, urgent and instant clearing
Payment codes, reference models with check digits, payment symbols
Payer tax ID, revenue type, municipality code, reference format; triggered by treasury creditor accounts
Central bank codes for payments with non-residents, above thresholds
Local letters allowed or not; local length limits
Local clearing calendar from a static holiday file
Restrictions on foreign-currency payments between residents

blocks.p: Illustrative examples for the packs. They come from general market knowledge, not from the CMIplus guidelines, and must be confirmed with each network bank.

head: Country
Examples
rows: Domestic EUR follows SEPA rules; IBAN 20 characters
CZK domestic; local account "prefix-number/bank code" with mod-11 check; variable, constant and specific symbols numeric (max 10, 4, 10 digits)
EUR SEPA domestic; variable, specific and constant symbols numeric, carried in EndToEndId as /VS…/SS…/KS…
HUF domestic; account 2×8 or 3×8 digits, each block with its own check digit; IBAN 28
RON domestic; IBAN mandatory (24); payments to State Treasury accounts (TREZ in the IBAN) need the payer's fiscal code
EUR SEPA domestic; HR reference models (HRnn) with model-specific check digits; IBAN 21
RSD domestic; 18-digit account with mod-97 control digits; 3-digit payment code mandatory; reference model 97 check digits
BAM domestic; 16-digit account with check digits; public revenue payments need taxpayer ID, payment and revenue type, municipality and reference
UAH domestic; IBAN 29; beneficiary tax ID (8 or 10 digits) and purpose text mandatory; budget payments in a prescribed purpose format

blocks.p: The country list itself needs confirming against the current CMIplus rollout.

In the app the country packs are still empty, so no Stage 8 rule runs yet. Each country file holds the currency, IBAN length, SEPA membership, character set (basic Latin for all 11) and accepted versions (.03 and .09 for all 11 until confirmed). SEPA membership set in the app: AL, AT, CZ, HR, HU, RO, RS and SK yes; BA, UA and XK no.
Stage 9 compares transactions and blocks with each other inside the uploaded file; it cannot see files already processed in production.

rows.check: PmtInfId unique in the file
InstrId unique in the file
EndToEndId unique in the file, except NOTPROVIDED
UETR (in .09) unique in the file
Possible duplicate transactions: same creditor account, amount, currency, date and remittance
Debtor account equal to creditor account
rows.app: Yes; not when both account currencies are given and differ (sub-accounts of one IBAN)

rows.check: Same debtor account in blocks with different debtor names
Same debtor account, date and payment type spread over several blocks
MsgId already used in a file this customer validated in the app before (app history only)
rows.app: Not built: the app keeps no history

rows.check: Ultimate debtor identical to the debtor

blocks.p: Stage 10 never rejects; it tells the customer what CMIplus would change, ignore or handle sub-optimally.

rows.check: Execution date on a weekend or local holiday; CMIplus moves it to the next business day
rows.app: Yes: weekends and TARGET closing days for EUR; no country holidays set yet; not for SEPA Instant or past dates
rows.built: Schematron + JS: payment type, business days

rows.check: Execution date is today and may miss the cut-off (indicative, from configured cut-off times)
rows.app: Off: no cut-off times set yet
rows.built: Schematron + JS: payment type, business days, cut-off time

rows.check: Text will be truncated by CMIplus or a downstream scheme
rows.app: Off: no CMIplus lengths set yet; downstream truncation is 7.25

rows.check: Characters will be transliterated
Elements present but ignored by CMIplus
Recommended data missing: structured creditor address, purpose code, LEI, ultimate debtor for payments on behalf
rows.app: Yes for the structured creditor address and the ultimate debtor; purpose code and LEI are off

rows.check: Hybrid address used where fully structured is recommended
pain.001.001.03 used; migration to .09 recommended if CMIplus plans to retire .03
rows.app: Yes, where the country also accepts .09

rows.check: File close to the size or transaction limits
rows.app: Off: no limits set yet; the file size is not checked because the CMIplus limit is not known

rows.check: Initiating party differs from debtor; check the ultimate debtor rules for payments on behalf
EndToEndId is NOTPROVIDED: send your own reference so the creditor gets one

blocks.p: This catalogue was confirmed on 18 Nov 2026 as the source of the app's rules; these decisions were made while the app was built and reviewed. Each is a setting or a rule change and is to be confirmed with the bank's files.

head: Date
Checks
Decision
rows: Warning instead of error: a payment between two accounts in one country in a foreign currency, such as USD in CZ, may be allowed.
New case: a cross-border payment without a debtor or creditor postal address is a warning.
Intra-bank and budget payments travel with the other payments of a block and do not make it mixed.
SEPA is derived from EUR and the countries only without any service level; EUR with G001, NURG or URGP is cross-border or domestic.
One problem, one finding: blank names only in 4.15 (and 4.5, 4.19, 4.32); 3.4 only when 3.2 and 3.3 are switched off; a currency that is not ISO only in 4.23; 4.31 not for cheques.
A file older than one month is a warning; a creation time more than 1 hour ahead stays an error.
Unstructured addresses are accepted with warnings 7.8 and 7.18; 4.30 rejects them only if that setting is switched off. An address with only Ctry and AdrLine counts as unstructured.
More than 2 address lines is reported by 6.3 only; the address-lines part of 4.30 is switched off.
Error for SEPA by service level and for SEPA Instant; a warning for a EUR payment between SEPA countries without service level, which the bank may send another way.
An urgent EUR payment (URGP, SDVA or priority HIGH) is domestic urgent or cross-border, not SEPA.
Reported once: the charges account IBAN by 4.18 (not 5.6), a missing creditor agent by 4.26 (not 7.17), the regulatory reporting country by 4.40 (not 5.10).
Left to other checks with the current settings: currencies to 7.1, 7.10 and 7.13; names to 6.4; remittance parts to 4.38.
Cannot fire: a creditor IBAN of another country makes the payment cross-border. Kept as a guard.
No file-size part: the CMIplus size limit is not known.
Limits, code lists and CMIplus guideline values are settings with a default, changeable per country; an empty setting switches its check off.
Added in the app's first version: 2.x for schema errors that 2.1–2.11 do not name, X.1 as a hint for EndToEndId NOTPROVIDED.

blocks.p: Not built in the app: 0.4, 0.6, 0.10, 1.5 and 1.6 (need CMIplus input or are not possible in the browser), 5.9 (no BIC directory) and 9.9 (no history).

The result mirrors a pain.002 technical check: a status per transaction, per payment block and for the file, each with the reason codes of its findings ([ISO status codes](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@taprsvp/iso20022_external_codes@1.0.1/code_sets/external_payment_group_status_code.json)).

head: Level
ACTC
ACWC
PART
RJCT
rows: No errors, but CMIplus would change data (e.g. date moved)
At least one error on it or inherited from its block or file
Some transactions rejected (only if CMIplus accepts partially)
Block-level error, or all transactions rejected
Stage 0–2 structural error, group header error, or everything rejected

blocks.p: Whether CMIplus accepts files partially or rejects them as a whole is a per-country setting of the status logic.

In the app there is no PART status yet: an error anywhere in a block rejects the block, and any error rejects the file. Exports are a CSV of findings and a printable HTML report, plus a summary to share without payment data; the pain.002-like XML is not built.
The report contains:

ul: Summary: file name, version, selected country, number of blocks and transactions, totals per currency, overall status, counts of errors, warnings and hints.
Findings grouped by level and rule, filterable by severity and stage, with the derived payment type per transaction.
Exports: pain.002-like XML with statuses and reason codes, a PDF or HTML report for the customer, and a CSV or Excel list of findings.
Message texts from a translation catalogue keyed by rule ID: English first, local languages for phase 2.

blocks.p: These checks need production systems or customer data and stay out of phase 1; the report should say so, so customers do not read an ACTC as a guarantee of execution.

ul: Account existence and status (closed, blocked) and that the debtor account belongs to the customer
Customer contract, entitlements, signatures and authorisation workflow
Funds and customer-specific limits
Sanctions, AML and fraud screening
Verification of Payee for euro payments
Duplicate check against files already processed in production
Live reachability of the creditor bank for SEPA Instant
Live FX rates and FX contract validation
Binding cut-off times (only indicative in Stage 10)

blocks.p: Static reference data keeps phase 1 free of integrations: IBAN registry, BIC directory, ISO code lists, local bank directories and holiday calendars, versioned as configuration and refreshed by an admin process.
The selected country is the country the payments are sent to for processing; the RBI network bank operating there executes the file in CMIplus.

tasks.text: Confirm the meaning of the selected country. If it means the beneficiaries' country, Stage 8 would run per transaction by creditor country instead of once per file.
Confirm per country whether CMIplus accepts files partially or rejects them as a whole.
Align severities and reason codes with what CMIplus returns in its pain.002 today. Until then the app uses the proposals here, with the changes under Decisions after confirmation.
Confirm which pain.001 versions each country accepts and any retirement date for .03. The app accepts .03 and .09 for all 11 countries until then.
Confirm how CMIplus treats unstructured addresses in .03 and .09 files now that the November 2026 end dates are postponed. The app accepts them with warnings 7.8 and 7.18.
Decide the character set policy per country (local letters allowed or transliterated). The app uses basic Latin for all 11 countries for now; local letters get warning 5.2.
Set file size and transaction count limits. The app takes files up to 20 MB (browser limit); with no transaction or block limits set, 6.5 and 10.9 are off.
Name the owner and refresh cycle of static reference data, including the BIC directory licence. The app keeps its reference lists as files refreshed by a script and has no BIC directory.
Decide which warnings are shown to customers in phase 2.
